stories.headline: Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão remains integral part of Chelsea plans despite limited minutes
stories.summary: Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão remains an important part of his plans despite limited opportunities for the young Brazilian so far.
stories.body:
Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão remains an important part of his plans despite limited opportunities for the young Brazilian so far.

Estevao has made brief substitute appearances in two of Chelsea's three Premier League matches, coming close to earning a draw with champions Arsenal on Sunday with a late shot that was saved by David Raya.

The 19-year-old made 12 starts in the Premier League last season and scored eight goals in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

Alonso said in quotes reported by the Evening Standard: "Este is ready, he's training well. [Against Arsenal] he had a very good impact, he has a great chance. So he's fully involved and with a very good attitude every day."

"100% [he has an important role], because of his potential, because he's so young, but he's in that process to adapt and to learn quickly. And the season is going to be long."

Asked whether he had discussed the situation with the teenager, the Chelsea boss added: "Private conversations should remain private.

"The players that have the desire and the hunger to prove and to show every day that they are up for the challenge, it's what we want to create here in the building.

"And Este is part of it. So he has had a very good attitude, very good mentality to prepare every game and to be ready for the team."

- Alonso: Chelsea team is not close to being final product

- Premier League clubs are overspending on wingers who can't score goals

Chelsea will look to bounce back from their first competitive loss under Alonso when they take on Leeds in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday.

The Blues have received a boost with the availability of defender Levi Colwill, who remained on the bench during the defeat against Arsenal because of a fitness issue.

However, Moisés Caicedo remains unavailable along with summer signings Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Jordan Henderson.

Caicedo and Palestra are the closest to full fitness, but Alonso said on Chelsea's website: "They are still not ready to go, and it's not the moment to take an early risk. So we go game by game with them, but it's too early."

Right-back Palestra, who arrived from Atalanta in July, looked strong in preseason only to suffer an injury on the eve of the new campaign.

"It's especially [frustrating] for him," said Alonso. "He came with huge energy, huge desire to enjoy his game in the Premier League.

"He had a very good pre-season and, a few days before the first game against Fulham, he picked up an injury.

"It's part of the life of a football player to come back from injury and we will need him for sure. He has great potential and will add a lot of good qualities we need in the team."

It is the third time in four seasons that Chelsea and Leeds have clashed in cup competitions, with Chelsea coming out on top in the FA Cup in the fifth round in 2024 and the semi-finals in April.

Leeds have not won at Stamford Bridge since a 2-0 victory in the Premier League in December 1999.

stories.headline: Under pressure: those with the biggest questions to answer in the semis
stories.summary: Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. And that means a host of individuals, players and coaches are under pressure. Rohan Connolly looks at who has the biggest questions to answer.
stories.body:
Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. That's the equation. And that means a host of individuals, players, and coaches are ... under pressure (yep, that Queen/David Bowie classic's going through my head now, too).

Go on, put it on and click your fingers to that bassline while you read about those most under the pump on Friday and Saturday evening.

Justin Longmuir
You won't find too many better recent examples of one result so starkly changing the narrative surrounding an AFL coach than Fremantle's loss to Hawthorn last Thursday night. Longmuir and his team had done everything right this season until then. Yet the bottom line remains they now teeter on the edge of a straight sets exit at home with Longmuir copping plenty of critical flak. The Dockers' ball movement was stymied, they were inefficient, with 57 forward entries producing only five goals, and Hawthorn created space far too easily. The "lack of flexibility" accusation has also popped up again, along with more talk about costly poor starts. Fremantle lost a home final last year to Gold Coast. A third home finals defeat in a row could damage Longmuir's reputational stocks irreparably.

Jeremy Cameron
There may not be another player under as much pressure to perform on Friday night as the dual Coleman medallist, who has been goalless for a month, and five times in his last seven outings. Cameron took just one mark and had only nine disposals against Carlton last week, lacked any sort of physical presence, and was drifting up around the wing to pick up what few touches he could manage. Cameron managed two goals in Geelong's narrow Round 15 loss to Fremantle in Perth, but even then the Cats were held to the second-lowest score of their last 10 outings. Anything less this week, and there will be an awful lot of responsibility upon the likes of Shannon Neale and Patrick Dangerfield to find Cameron's missing goals.

Josh Treacy
What's that expression, one day a rooster the next a feather duster? On August 25, Fremantle's Josh Treacy was being feted as the All-Australian centre half-forward for 2026. Just over a week later, he was getting towelled up by the critics for being "destroyed" by Hawthorn key defender Josh Battle. Treacy had just four disposals, no marks and kicked just one late consolation goal. He hadn't had a kick until late in the last quarter and was accused of not attacking the contest with his usual physical presence. It doesn't get any easier this week for him, either, given that last time Fremantle met Geelong, Connor O'Sullivan held him to 2.2 from only nine disposals, picking up 16 himself, six intercept marks and a coaches' vote. Treacy needs to improve on that effort and last week's significantly.

Patrick Dangerfield
Hang on. How can the best player on the ground in last week's elimination final be under pressure the very next game he plays? Well, being the long-time acknowledged champion he is, the Brownlow medallist is always under the microscope to an extent. If "Danger" plays a blinder, Geelong will generally win. That's pressure of its own. But then there's the memory of last year. Prior to last Friday night, it was in the 2025 preliminary final against Hawthorn that Dangerfield delivered his best September performance with 31 disposals and three goals. And the following week? Unfortunately, his banged-up 35-year-old frame couldn't repeat the dose, delivering a strangely muted 10-disposal effort in the grand final loss to Brisbane. Now, 12 months older, can he back up one superlative September effort with another?

Murphy Reid
Last year's Rising Star and this year's All-Australian might be a bit of a soft target given what he's done in two seasons, that he's only recently turned 20 and last week played only his second AFL final, but Reid was one of the biggest disappointments in Fremantle's soft qualifying final performance. Whether missing the two games prior with a groin niggle has thrown him out of his stride is an interesting question, but his usually precise kicking was unusually off-target against the Hawks, and his off night was a major factor in Fremantle lacking so much of the spark the headbanded youngster has brought to the team and which had typified their season to date.

Lachie Neale
The dual Brownlow medallist was hardly the only Lion to have a poor one last week, but there's several reasons he's probably under more pressure than nearly all his teammates this week. Most obviously, given the widespread expectation that he's headed elsewhere in 2027, this could well be his final game for the club. Plus he and the other midfielders are coming off a pantsing by the Swans and, in Neale's case, Jai Serong. Even if the Lions are to get through this, Neale remains under pressure; Brisbane would face the all-conquering Hawks, before potentially the Swans again or an old September foe in Geelong, with tagger Oisin Mullin looming as another handbrake on the two-time Brownlow winner. Neale's record in finals overall is stellar, but Brisbane has seldom needed one of his best September performances more.

Matthew Nicks
OK, let's be clear, Nicks isn't going to lose his job if Adelaide can't pull an upset against Brisbane at the Gabba, even though he might have had the Crows not beaten the Bulldogs last week. But pressure? That hasn't suddenly evaporated just because a rested Adelaide beat a lesser-ranked opponent at home and gave Nicks his first finals win. The stigma of last year's straight sets elimination remains strong, the Crows won three fewer games this season and finished five spots lower on the ladder, and their record against the very best in 2026 is hardly inspiring, 2-5 against the top five, including a 52-point thumping at the hands of Saturday's opponent at the same venue. Victory this time would absolutely shore up Nicks' credentials. Another bad loss? The question marks will intensify.

Brisbane's key defenders
Saturday was a horror show for the whole Brisbane line-up, but no-one more than its defenders, and its talls in Harris Andrews, Darcy Gardiner and Ryan Lester specifically, with Sydney pair Charlie Curnow and Logan McDonald booting 11 goals between them. McDonald successfully curbed Andrews' intercepting ability and cashed in with half-a-dozen goals, and Curnow smashed Gardiner. And the equation doesn't get any easier this week with Adelaide's three-pronged tall forward set-up featuring Riley Thilthorpe, Taylor Walker and Darcy Fogarty, who StatMate tells us has kicked at least two goals in his last eight games. Ty Gallop surely is a good chance of returning at Gardiner's expense, or even second ruck Darcy Fort. But whatever selection strings coach Chris Fagan pulls, the Lions can't afford their key backs to be anywhere near that bad again.

stories.headline: Lakers to unveil statue of Hall of Fame coach Phil Jackson
stories.summary: The Lakers are honoring legendary coach Phil Jackson with a statue to be unveiled outside Crypto.com Arena on April 9.
stories.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers will honor Phil Jackson -- who won five of his unprecedented 11 NBA coaching titles in L.A. -- with a statue next season, the team announced Tuesday.

"Phil Jackson defines championship basketball for a reason," Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss said in a statement. "His masterful approach to coaching brought out the best in some of the greatest athletes to ever play the game. After he accepted my dad's invitation to join the Lakers, Phil's unmatched creativity and commitment to excellence restored our championship legacy, bringing five titles and setting a standard of excellence for generations to come.

"It is a great joy to be able to mark that achievement with the statue he so richly deserves."

The statue will be unveiled April 9, 2027, before the Lakers' game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Jackson, 80, coached the Lakers for 11 seasons across two stints (1999-2004, 2005-11), winning three championships running his patented triangle offense through Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal as the team's primary stars and two more with Bryant and Pau Gasol as L.A.'s lynchpins.

Jackson guided the Lakers to titles in five of seven trips to the NBA Finals, winning in three-peat fashion from 2000-02 and adding back-to-back rings in 2009 and 2010.

Jackson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2007 and was named as one of the 15 greatest coaches in NBA history when the league revealed its coaching selections as part of its 75th anniversary season.

Jackson will be the ninth member of the Lakers with a statue at Star Plaza outside Crypto.com Arena, joining Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Elgin Baylor, Chick Hearn, Magic Johnson, Pat Riley, Jerry West, O'Neal and Bryant (who has two).

The statue was commissioned by the Lakers to be designed and created by Omri Amrany of Rotblatt Amrany Studio.

stories.headline: Germany beats South Korea, rolls into World Cup quarterfinals
stories.summary: Host Germany advanced to the quarterfinals of the women's FIBA World Cup with a morale-boosting 94-56 rout of South Korea on Tuesday, and the United States learned its next opponent.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- Host Germany advanced to the quarterfinals of the women's FIBA World Cup with a morale-boosting 94-56 rout of South Korea on Tuesday, and the United States learned its next opponent.

Hungary, which beat Japan 84-63, will play the four-time defending champion U.S. on Thursday.

Germany captain Marie Gülich led her team to a quarterfinal against European champion Belgium with 19 points and five rebounds.

Every German score elicited huge cheers from the appreciative home fans at the Berlin Arena, particularly in the first half. Germany led by 17 points at halftime.

The home team has been gradually improving since losing its first group game by 30 points to Spain. Germany rebounded with a 74-58 win over Japan and followed with an 83-58 win over Mali.

Hungary eliminates Japan Réka Lelik led Hungary with 23 points and eight rebounds in a surprisingly comfortable win over Japan earlier.

Virág Takács-Kiss also had eight rebounds and added 17 points for Hungary, which will face the U.S. in the late quarterfinal slot Thursday.

"It feels incredible. It's been 40 years since we went to the quarterfinals and I still can't believe it," Lelik said.

The game was overshadowed by a serious injury to Japan shooting guard Saki Hayashi, who went off with what looked a broken right arm after an awkward fall.

Hayashi needed immediate medical attention a foul in the air from Agnes Torok with just over a minute left in the second quarter. A blue tarp was provided to give her privacy and fans responded with applause when she was led off.

Japan connected on only seven 3-pointers Tuesday. The Japanese had set a record with 20 three-pointers in a World Cup game on Friday before France broke it with 22 on Monday.

Ramu Tokashiki's two free throws drew Japan level at 34-34, but that was as close as it got. Agnes Studer responded with a 3-pointer to give Hungary a 37-34 lead at halftime.

"They hit their open shots, we missed our open shots," Japan coach Corey Gaines said.

Hungary finished 11 of 25 from beyond the arc on the first of two days off for the U.S., which qualified directly for the quarterfinals as a group winner.

"I'm excited to play the very best players in the world, the best team in the word," Lelik said of Thursday's game. "I never got the opportunity to play against them. So I'm just very excited how it's going to be. And we're going to do everything for sure. But besides that, I want us to enjoy the game."

Still two places up for grabs All the quarterfinals are scheduled for Thursday. Spain and France await the winners of Wednesday's playoffs between Italy-Australia and China-Puerto Rico, respectively.

George Russell has got his wish after his grandstand joust with Lando Norris at Silverstone.

The Mercedes man has followed in his McLaren rival's footsteps as Silverstone announced the George Russell Grandstand would be opened at the circuit's Farm Curve for next year's race.

Norris debuted his 'Landostand' in 2025 when he claimed his maiden British Grand Prix win and this year 16,000 fans packed it out at Stowe corner.

Russell revealed his desire to also have a grandstand for his own race and quipped during this year's Silverstone weekend that he quite fancied taking some of Norris' seats.

"Good luck," Norris retorted. "I have more passionate fans and a better fanbase I think. Mine was more wanted from a public point of view, which is a great thing.

stories.headline: How to draft, play and win your fantasy hockey league like an expert
stories.summary: It's not just who you draft, it's everything that happens after. An expert guide to play fantasy hockey like the pros.
stories.body:
Let's go! Coming off a long summer following one of the most exciting hockey seasons ever, on and off the NHL ice, we're ready to re-embrace the game we love, as both fans and invested fantasy managers. Whether you're a wily veteran or brand new to the game, we're here to help you not only compete but give yourself a solid shot at victory. Starting with this primer that serves as an introduction for newbies and a refresher for those more well-versed.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

The draft

The most important two hours of your entire fantasy hockey season. But don't sweat it! A little research and preparation is all it takes to cobble together a competitive roster. To start, don't overcomplicate matters, take the best player available. This year, that's Nathan MacKinnon, Nikita Kucherov, Macklin Celebrini, or Connor McDavid (yes, even under new defensive-minded head coach Mike Babcock).

Once that elite quartet is off the board, turn to the second tier of elite forwards including Leon Draisaitl, Jason Robertson, and David Pastrnak. Your blue line and net can wait a moment. Cale Makar isn't fetching you fantasy points for dollars earned and there are enough good-to-great goalies even once Andrei Vasilevskiy is off the table. Grab your big scorer up front, first and foremost. These are the skaters who can average 3.0-plus per game in ESPN standard points leagues.

Use the next few early rounds to acquire at least one premiere fantasy defenseman and a top-tier netminder (more on those positions below), while always keeping an eye out for the remaining gems up front. Don't fret about filling positional requirements at this stage and continue to grab the heavy hitters. I promise the fantasy math will eventually work out in your favor.

Okay, once the best players are off the board, and your top-tier goalie is secured, now start working to satisfy positional and categorical needs. Too many right-wingers will result in too many quality performers stuck on your bench on busier nights. While a dearth at another position is also frustratingly limiting. Of course, if your league adheres to the overarching (F) classification, continue to draft the best player available. In later rounds, it's time to really focus on sleepers, bounce-back and breakout contenders. These potential pleasant surprises can truly alter a roster for the better.

Back to the importance of research and preparation, as usual, we're here to help with preseason previews covering all matters fantasy hockey right up until your draft and beyond.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Bounce-back and breakout candidates

With the top center in San Jose serving as the poster child for breakout candidates in 2025-26, Celebrini wasn't alone in taking a leap forward. The Anaheim Ducks' Cutter Gauthier impressed us with his 41-goal statement season just as (then) Tampa Bay Lightning defender Darren Raddysh won over alert managers by finishing 11th in fantasy points, despite missing nine games. Cole Caufield followed linemate Nick Suzuki's lead from the previous season by exploding for 88 points, including 51 goals. Will linemate Juraj Slafkovsky be next in busting through the 80-point mark? Meanwhile in Philadelphia, Dan Vladar proved he does indeed have the chops to serve as a No. 1 netminder. Easier said than done, but spotting these characters before they erupt can go a long way to ameliorating your fantasy squad.

Zach Benson of the Buffalo Sabres could be one such candidate, after making such a positive impression this past spring. Poised to see top-line minutes alongside Tage Thompson, the scrappy winger feels on the verge of going next-level. Celebrini's roommate, Will Smith is also in ideal position to erupt at age 21. On the blue line, I like Cole Hutson of the Washington Capitals to wow us as a rookie, and Jet Greaves is in position to finally establish himself as a prominent fantasy netminder for the Columbus Blue Jackets.

As for bounce-back performers, goalie Jeremy Swayman and forward Ryan O'Reilly are just two examples of figures who rebounded off rather drab campaigns the previous year. Now I have my sights set on Tampa Bay's Brayden Point and Capitals newbie Jordan Kyrou to do the same. Elias Pettersson is an intriguing figure -- altogether not a bad fantasy performer despite his disappointing play in Vancouver -- as someone who might finally get back to the player he was under new management and a fresh coaching staff. The former 100-point forward very much might be worth a roll of the fantasy dice.

Less appealing "B" candidates

Backsliders. Maybe they're coming off a season that's just too anomalous and tough to duplicate. Age could be another factor, along with a new role within the lineup or on another team altogether. Whatever the reason, these players are moving in the wrong direction production-wise, and you want to avoid them.

Boston's Morgan Geekie potted 25 goals in his first 36 games and then just another 14 in the following 45 contests. Managers unfamiliar with that timing and trend might be unjustifiably wooed by the total of 39 and mistake the winger for a 40-goal scorer. When in reality, even if he remains on a top line with Pastrnak, the 28-year-old sports true 30-goal potential at heart.

Does Alex DeBrincat score another 40-plus with Patrick Kane back in Chicago? Considering that loss and the state of hockey with the Detroit Red Wings at present, I wouldn't predict as much. Sure, ex-Sabre Alex Tuch could flirt with the 35-goal and 70-point mark once more on a line with Dylan Strome and Alex Ovechkin in Washington, or enjoy more modest numbers on another unit. Just as some players are going to improve statistically with a different supporting cast, others will move in the opposite direction, and expectations should be tempered.

This isn't to suggest you shouldn't draft Geekie, DeBrincat, Tuch and others, just don't jump on them too early with the mind you're getting last year's exact fantasy model.

More on goalies

You won't win your league, or even make a go of it, with bad fantasy goaltending. Snoozing on this position is not an option. These few competitors are responsible for far too many categories. So as tempting as it may be to snag another high-performing skater when it's the right time to address your needs in net, take the latter route.

The first rule of thumb is to avoid netminders on lousy teams. Arguably the best goaltender in the world played 57 games for a surprisingly bad squad in Winnipeg this past season. By the time mid-April rolled around, Connor Hellebuyck netted his managers fewer fantasy points than 27 others in the league. Taking large personal strides, Spencer Knight served as a promising figure for the Blackhawks through yet another rebuilding campaign in Chicago. Yet despite making 22 more starts than Jesper Wallstedt in Minnesota, Knight still finished well below the Wild netminder in the fantasy standings. No matter how individually talented, great goalies on an inferior teams most often aren't in position to regularly reward their managers.

But busy is good too. Once zoned in on the better teams in the league, it's wise to target those who play the most. Tampa Bay's Vasilevskiy is a great example, as is Dallas Stars netminder Jake Oettinger. Logan Thompson presents as a top-five fantasy netminder, again, on a Capitals team that should be even better. While the league continues to trend in the direction of relying on two or more figures between the pipes, there's still a good number of goalies who carry a significantly heavier workload. Such characters on quality squads need to be chased, first and foremost.

After your top performers are secured, give prominent starters on improving teams and top-tier tandem members a look. It's Greaves' net in Columbus. If the Blue Jackets can equal or improve-upon their record from this past run, the 25-year-old will prove valuable. As for old faces in new places, ex-New Jersey Devils netminder Jacob Markstrom could be in for nice rebound campaign with the Florida Panthers.

Colorado's Scott Wedgewood reigns supreme as member of the tandem crowd, while Stanley Cup Champ Brandon Bussi should see more starts than Pyotr Kotchetkov now that Frederik Andersen is in Edmonton. The options open up considerably, again, once your recognized heavy-hitters are in place.

For more on how to address this all-important position, check out our dedicated goalie preview.

A slightly deeper dive on D-men

Unlike in years past, Makar is no longer a list of one as far as premier fantasy defenders are concerned. Six blueliners -- Makar, Zach Werenski, Evan Bouchard, Moritz Seider, Charlie McAvoy and Jake Sanderson -- all averaged between 2.4 and 2.6 fantasy points/game in ESPN standard leagues this past season. While Makar and Bouchard sit a titch above the rest, the gap is much smaller than before. Another good throng, including Quinn Hughes, Rasmus Dahlin and Lane Hutson, banged out 2.2 points/game in 2025-26. In most leagues, you want at least one top-tier performer, along with a pair from that secondary, yet still impressive, sub-set. Then take a breath.

In competition that rewards blocked-shots, there's no real sense of urgency in padding your fantasy roster with defenders. This past campaign, 29 blueliners earned between 1.7 and 2.1 fantasy points/game. Plenty to go around. Instead, pursue skaters that are going to put up the flashiest numbers first, regardless of position. Of course, as with every position, when rounding out your defensive corps, keep an eye out for prospective breakout candidates. The Los Angeles Kings' Brandt Clarke and Capitals rookie Cole Hutson are two such names on my 2026-27 radar.

Leagues, leagues, leagues

As for customization, ESPN Fantasy provides the forum to create any type of league you want. If interested in constructing your own head-to-head competition, first settle on either the points or categories path, then determine the applicable stats. Beyond scoring, hits and blocked-shots -- to reward defensive play -- are more popular than ever. Maybe you're a faceoff enthusiast, and want to compensate the best and busiest in the dot. Have a penchant for penalty minutes? PIM remains an option, along with a good variety of others to suit your fantasy hockey tastes. Managers who don't care to customize can always opt for our default head-to-head points league, referenced above, which remains widely popular.

For those who want to kick it old school, Rotisserie (Roto) competition awards points based on where your players rank as a collective in every category. For instance, in a 12-team league, the group of skaters that boasts the most total goals, at any given time, retain the maximum 12 points. The fantasy team with the worst plus/minus receives just one. And so on, cumulatively and fluidly, through each category to arrive at a combined sum. H2H category leagues differ from points leagues in that not only one goal, but one hit or one blocked-shot, can mean the difference between victory and defeat regarding that particular stat. Scores carry forward and add up throughout the campaign -- say, 6-4, then 3-7 etc. -- unlike in a head-to-head points battle where you either win the week or you don't.

Once the parameters and makeup of your league are set, decide how much time you want to invest in adjusting your lineup. Every day, every week, or never again, in honor of how we used to pen-and-paper-it back in the pre-internet days of yore.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Categories matter

Becoming intimately acquainted with your league's specific categories is essential to success. Not only with the stats themselves, but how much weight they carry. One hit in category leagues makes a greater impact than when only worth 0.1 points otherwise. If assists are equivalent to goals, Lane Hutson is nearly equal to Makar as a fantasy performer. Conversely, a sniper like Steven Stamkos (at least in his second season with the Nashville Predators) boasts a lot more shine in fantasy competition where goals double helpers in value. If blocked-shots don't count, a defender like Toronto's Jake McCabe belongs nowhere near your fantasy roster. Anyway, you get the idea.

Investing in mock drafts

The more you mock draft, the better. While practice doesn't necessarily make perfect in this case, it certainly helps. These dress rehearsals will offer you insight as to how other managers are navigating the draft along with player preferences. If everyone is avoiding a high-ranked skater there's likely a reason why. You'll also be better prepared for certain trends -- a too-early run on goalies, for instance -- after experiencing one for pretend. Plus, they're fun. Check out our Mock Draft Lobby, pick the room that best represents your own fantasy league, and take a spin.

Not sure how to play? Try out the ESPN Mock Draft Lobby.

Building a dynasty

This style of fantasy competition suits those who want to play the long game. Most akin to the real-life NHL affair, managing a dynasty hockey squad requires patience and foresight. Barring trades, you're stuck with these players, like it or not, for the haul. Last season, I recommended grabbing Matthew Schaefer right off the top, even if he didn't end up playing in the NHL full-time (a laughable concept now). This year, that's Leafs No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna, who is expected to suit up right away. Our fantasy rookie rundown will further help with who to target for what's likely to be a long, and hopefully happy, dynasty fantasy marriage.

Keeper leagues are different in that you're able to jettison your lesser players each season and keep only those most treasured. How to approach the draft in rounding out your roster largely depends on your club's current state. Are you rich with peak talent and ready to win now? Then go on and grab some aging veterans to help with that championship push. Otherwise, if your team is still also in the building phase, similar to many real NHL clubs, it's wiser to invest in younger, gifted players who sport the wherewithal to be great down the road.

Roster maintenance

This is the fun part. Outside of set-and-forget leagues, how well you fiddle with your roster will determine whether you're still in the championship hunt once spring rolls around, or already looking ahead to next season. Striking the right balance is of ultimate importance, as too much tinkering -- for instance losing patience with an underperforming player and prematurely letting them go -- can also bite you in the behind.

Even before puck-drop on day one, it's essential to become familiar with your pool of available free agents. I guarantee a few will emerge as valuable fantasy performers in those first few weeks, or even days. Whether their success is due to an unexpected line assignment or another factor. Trust me, these players will already be rostered by the most vigilant managers before others even realize what's going on. To repeat, the first few weeks of the season are absolutely integral in allowing you the chance to improve your roster, by swapping in unanticipated performers for your lesser draft choices.

With so few candidates available, goalies are especially important to monitor early on. Raise your hand if you had Carolina Hurricanes waiver pickup Brandon Bussi on your fantasy roster to start 2025-26. Right. After going 31-6-2 (2.44 GAA) in the regular season, the 28-year-old Stanley Cup champion is now considered a top-15 fantasy netminder heading into 2026-27. Your responsibility is to identify this season's Bussi and snag him before anyone else.

One last tip on roster maintenance: Set every day's lineup at the start of the week. You can always shift players around later, but at least there's a reasonable lineup in place if you can't address it for a day or two.

A word on injured reserve

Use those IR slots to your advantage, beginning with the draft. You can always move out such inactive players for others, if necessary, once the league is in full swing. For instance, in all but the shallowest of leagues, Seth Jarvis should be accounted for on draft day, even though he's not expected back from shoulder surgery until November or December. The Carolina forward checks too many fantasy boxes, too well, to leave on the board. The boost he'll provide your squad, once back to health, could prove tangibly beneficial once we're into the meat of the season.

Similarly to the real-life game, it's like trading for a quality player mid-season without giving anything up (other than dumping your biggest roster disappointment). The same applies to Chicago's Connor Bedard, Edmonton's Frederik Andersen, and others. Fill up those IR slots with banged-up placeholders in later stages of your draft. If you need to pivot and jettison Jarvis later because Nathan MacKinnon suffers an injury, so be it.

The art of trades

In my decades of covering and playing fantasy hockey, I've noticed that the most active managers are often the most successful. That goes beyond working the wire. Particularly in deeper leagues, trades are a great way to improve your roster when there's an obvious weakness. Such deals are not tools used to scam another manager. Ideally, both partners come away filling a void. Your goalie for their high-performing winger etc. Maybe you need to address one specific categorical box, such as hits or blocked shots. If most of your fellow managers are trade wary, keep at it. You're likely to find a dance partner eventually. Unless this is you, start with those who are stuck with lousy goaltending. They're usually the most desperate.

With that, here's to a fantastic fantasy season in 2026-27. Good luck!

stories.headline: Pochettino cautious about young stars for USMNT camp amid buzz around Sullivan, Hall
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and NYRB's Julian Hall.
stories.body:
United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and Red Bull New York's Julian Hall.

The U.S. has scheduled a quartet of friendlies starting at the end of the month, starting with a match against Peru on Sept. 26, Chile on Sept. 29, Mexico on Oct. 3, and then Canada on Oct. 6. The roster will be announced on Sept. 17, with players beginning to arrive in Atlanta three days later.

As such there is much anticipation about what young players might get called up, including Sullivan and Hall.

Upon signing on for another World Cup cycle last month, Pochettino said he would be "starting from zero" in terms of building his team.

Speaking to reporters via video conference from London, Pochettino stressed he is trying to look at the potential of young players in a balanced way, and not let expectations get ahead of a player's development.

"I think we are very happy about to have all these potential good players being young, and with a possibility to perform and to play," Pochettino said.

"Only we need to be careful. We need to be careful because when you are young, of course you need to be confident, you need to have the trust in yourself, and believe that you can perform and you can do well. But the thing is it's a limit. The balance is the most important.

"And one of our responsibilities is to protect this guy because sometime if you play well and you are 17, 16 or 18 and you play well and people started to know to talk about that you are Messi or you are a big star in the world because you do some few good things. If after you are confused and you don't manage well, that can be dangerous for your career.

"And that is what we don't want. [We want] the young guys with potential being top players to provide the platform for them to evolve and to be professional, to build their career in the best way, improving every day, being humble, being careful when they talk in the media, when they talk with the teammate, when they talk with the opponent. I think respect is the most important thing and they need to be respectful. And of course we want players with talent."

Pochettino said that one goal for this cycle to further eradicate some bad habits that currently exist in the program.

Part of this the alignment of youth and professional clubs with the U.S. Soccer Federation.

The USSF recently announced a takeover of U.S. Youth Soccer.

"I think it's important when we talk about habits, it's about talking about everything, because after the player behave on the field because of this type of decision, they came from the top, he said.

"And we need to be aligned all together in our principles and all the concept that we need to improve if we want to be competitive in every single moment in our [path] until to the first team. I think we are all focused in trying to add our knowledge."

But Pochettino added that the bad habits also include players deciding not to take part competitive tournaments like the Gold Cup.

This a reference to players like Christian Pulisic who opted to sit out the 2025 Gold Cup in order to recover from a long club season.

"We were talking [about] the habit. Before it was difficult to make the roster for the World Cup one year before, because the mindset was different and say, 'Oh, if I play, I have not holidays, I cannot arrive fresh for the World Cup," Pochettino said.

"Already, with the time, you know now that is bulls--- -- sorry -- and I think it's to change this type of idea that are not right and that our experience to build mindset with the coaches, with the people in the organization, in the clubs, and of course us, and then the player that in the way that we will plan and we will do the things is the best for them, for the player, and it's going to be the best for soccer in the USA."

Pochettino added that despite the USMNT playing four games during the window, he will bring in his standard number of 26 players, including four goalkeepers.

Anything more than that would mean some players wouldn't get minutes.

"In this period of the season, we need to be careful with the player that we are going to call," he said.

"We need the players that we'll call that [they] be available to train, but also to play. And I think we consider it at the moment ,and to call 26 players with four keepers. And I think more than this is I think it's an issue because after to train, to share the minutes, I think the player that we are going to have, we want to see, we want to give the possibility to play ... with the possibility to compete. That is the idea for the next camp."

Pochettino indicated that some players who have just switched clubs, like the Middlesbrough duo of defender Max Arfsten and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, might not be called in in order to give them more time to settle into their new surroundings.

But he indicated there would be a balance between youth and experience.

"I think we cannot bring the whole squad [with] young players because they need to have some guys with experience already competing," Pochettino said.

"But yes, we are going to do a mix ... I think experienced player with young player that can fit together and start to work on how the young kid start to manage the pressure to play in the first team."

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail FW1: Fifita, Latrell feared the worst; Holmes set for World Cup
stories.summary: Blake Lawrie will earn a rare start this weekend before he heads off to join the Super League, while the future of his Dragons teammate Tyrell Sloan is still a little uncertain.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into Week 1 of the NRL finals.

Holmes set for World Cup despite injury

KL Iro has revealed Valentine Holmes is expecting to play for the Cook Islands, despite suffering a syndesmosis injury in the Dragons' last game of the year.

"I saw him yesterday," Iro shared.

"He had a moon boot on, but I think it's a low grade [injury].

"He told me he's sweet to go."

Both stars are expected to suit up for Cook Islands in this year's World Cup

Latrell feared season was over

Latrell Mitchell has revealed there were genuine doubts over whether he would play again this season as he battled the back injury that threatened to derail his finals return.

Mitchell revealed a bulging disc, which he had unknowingly carried for some time, flared during South Sydney's clash with Newcastle and left his return this year in doubt.

"To be fair, I didn't really know if I was gonna play again this year," Mitchell said.

"There were some times there where it definitely was questionable."

The Rabbitohs superstar said the issue became particularly painful during the Newcastle game, despite playing through the second half.

"Apparently I've had it for a very long time," Mitchell said.

"At half-time of the Newcastle Knights game, it was burning me."

Fifita feared career was slipping away
David Fifita has opened up on the "dark days" that left him questioning whether he could return to his destructive best following a string of ankle problems.

The Rabbitohs forward has rediscovered some of his most damaging football heading into the finals, but admitted multiple surgeries across 2024 and 2025 had him second-guessing what his future in the game looked like.

"I had some dark days, second guessing myself and thinking, 'Do I still have it?'" Fifita said.

"I had a few issues with my ankle at the end of 2024 and then... two or three surgeries in that period of time.

"You understand what goes through my head as a 24-year-old. People telling me this and that about my future in the sport."

Fifita said Wayne Bennett's faith has played a major role in rebuilding his confidence since joining South Sydney.

"I've just got a coach that backs me and loves me. I feel the love," he said.

"People thought I was done... and Wayne trusted me, believed in me."

Now preparing for his first finals appearance since 2021, Fifita believes his recent performances have provided the reassurance he needed.

"It reassured me that I still got it."

Finals take on special meaning for Fifita

David Fifita will carry extra motivation into South Sydney's finals campaign, with Friday marking an emotional period for the forward as the first anniversary of his father's death approaches.

Fifita revealed his father tragically passed on September 12 last year, describing the period as an incredibly difficult time for himself and his family.

"It was a very emotional time for my family and myself," Fifita said.

"People don't really know what I went through. To come down here at such a young age and leave all my family... it's very tough."

Fifita had initially planned to return home for the anniversary before South Sydney's finals qualification changed those plans.

"I was supposed to go up there and celebrate the one year, but obviously we're in finals now," he said.

"I'll be doing it for my family and my dad.

"I know my dad is looking [from] above, he's with me every step of the way... I do everything for him."

The 22-year-old has already committed his future to the Magpies and an announcement is expected later this week. Newcastle had been especially determined to keep Hall in the summer having already seen the departures of Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimarães and Sandro Tonali.

stories.headline: Kylian Mbappé: Want Champions League win 'more than anything,' more important than Ballon d'Or
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé said he wants to win the Champions League "more than anything" -- and that he'd prefer it to winning the Ballon d'Or -- after Real Madrid's 2-1 win over Inter on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Kylian Mbappé said he wants to win the Champions League "more than anything" -- and that he'd prefer it to winning the Ballon d'Or -- after Real Madrid's 2-1 win over Inter on Tuesday.

Mbappé and Federico Valverde put Madrid 2-0 up in the first half at the Bernabéu, taking advantage of two defensive mistakes from Inter, before Carlos Augusto pulled a goal back for the visitors in the second half.

Inter dominated the game for long periods, but Madrid took all three points in José Mourinho's first European game back at the club.

"That's the objective, that's the goal," Mbappé told CBS, when asked about lifting the Champions League this season. "That's what I said yesterday about the Ballon d'Or, but the Champions League is even more important. I play for the club of my dreams.

"It's really important for me to win the Champions League here in Madrid, I want it more than anything. But of course the Ballon d'Or this year, I think it's a great opportunity. It's a good year for me."

Mbappé has been nominated for the men's Ballon d'Or after scoring 10 goals at the World Cup this summer as France reached the semifinals.

However he has failed to win a major trophy with his club since arriving at Madrid two years ago.

Last season, Madrid were eliminated by Bayern Munich in the quarterfinals.

"We want to be a collective, we want to be a team who can compete with all the best teams in the world. We know that last year was a bit difficult for us in the Champions League.

"At Real Madrid you always have to be at the top, I hope this year we'll compete as a collective, to be where we want to be."

stories.headline: 49ers' Alfred Collins (knee) injured in practice, out for season
stories.summary: 49ers starting defensive tackle Alfred Collins suffered a torn patellar tendon in the team's Tuesday practice in Australia, an injury that will keep him out for the 2026 season.
stories.body:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- San Francisco 49ers starting defensive tackle Alfred Collins suffered a torn patellar tendon in the team's Tuesday practice in Australia, an injury that will keep him out for the 2026 season.

Coach Kyle Shanahan announced the injury Wednesday and confirmed that Collins will not return this year. That injury comes on the heels of defensive end Sam Okuayinonu landing on injured reserve with a broken foot that will require surgery over the weekend.

"Alfred tore his patellar tendon yesterday," Shanahan said. "That was a big loss. We've lost two D-lineman pretty much for the year after cuts and before the first game which has been a huge challenge. I'm hurting for Alfred... It was real unfortunate for him."

According to Shanahan, the injury happened in Tuesday's practice just before the team started 11-on-11 drills. Like Okuayinonu, Collins will also require surgery and go on injured reserve in the near future, ending his second season before it could start.

The Niners had big plans for Collins in 2026 after working him in as a rookie last season. Originally a second-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft, Collins played in 16 games last season, posting 17 tackles, a sack, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries.

Collins was one of the heroes of San Francisco's Week 5 win against the Los Angeles Rams, forcing and recovering a fumble at the Niners' 1-yard line to help preserve a fourth-quarter lead.

With Collins out of the mix, the Niners will enter Thursday night's season opener against the Rams with C.J. West and rookie Gracen Halton as the only healthy options on the 53-man roster who can start next to fellow defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa. Undrafted rookie James Thompson Jr. is another possibility, but he has missed practice with a hamstring issue.

The Niners do have a couple of practice squad options -- Sebastian Valdez and Kevin Givens -- with them in Melbourne whom they could elevate to play the Rams.

"Any D-lineman is a possibility unless you guys can name some guys we can fly here real quick," Shanahan said.

Elsewhere on the injury front, Shanahan confirmed that the team is aiming to play defensive end Nick Bosa (right ACL) and tight end George Kittle (right Achilles) against the Rams, though he also acknowledged they'll have to manage them closely in their first game back.

"We've got to be smart with that," Shanahan said. "Bosa not practicing as much, Kittle, he's had this whole week but they both look great. But we definitely have got to be smart with that."

stories.headline: Pelicans trade Jordan Hawkins to Grizzlies in 4-player deal
stories.summary: The Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round draft pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.
stories.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round draft pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

The trade, which was announced Tuesday, clears roster space for the Pelicans, frees up salary flexibility to sign Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal, and allows New Orleans to have a look at a young player in the 21-year-old Johnson, who was the No. 21 pick in the 2024 draft.

Hawkins, a lottery pick at No. 14 in the 2023 draft, now gets dealt by his team prior to his fourth season.

The Grizzlies, who picked up draft assets in the deal, will have multiple roster decisions before the start of the season as they are several guaranteed contracts above the 15 maximum.

Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

The Pelicans will be the fifth team in three seasons for the 6-foot-5 Johnson, who split last season between the Washington Wizards and Dallas Mavericks.

The Mavericks traded Johnson to the Grizzlies for Santi Aldama in July, five months after Johnson was included in the Anthony Davis blockbuster trade between Dallas and Washington. Johnson was drafted by the Milwaukee Bucks in 2024 before being traded later that season to the Wizards.

The trade saves New Orleans $5.7 million in salary, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks. Johnson was not allowed to be aggregated in a deal until Tuesday -- two months from the Aldama trade.

Gibson, 41, appeared in 10 games with Memphis last season. The 17-year veteran has played for eight different teams in his NBA career.

The 6-foot-7 Peavy appeared in 61 games as a rookie last season for the Pelicans, averaging 4.3 points.

stories.headline: Potential WNBA commissioner candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert
stories.summary: Executives from the WNBA, NBA and Nike are among potential candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert when she retires.
stories.body:
The WNBA is in search of a new leader, as commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday that she will retire at the end of the calendar year.

Engelbert is the sixth league head and second-longest tenured behind Val Ackerman. Engelbert is the first to hold the title of WNBA commissioner, as the previous leaders served as president.

The process to find Engelbert's replacement will start later this month, if not sooner, sources told ESPN. Presumably, the hire will be made by and report to NBA commissioner Adam Silver, as was the case with Engelbert. She told the Associated Press and The IX that she has been working on a succession plan for years, and that she has already submitted a list of potential internal and external candidates to Silver.

It is unclear who else might have input on the decision, though the Board of Governors is expected to be involved. Prior to hiring Engelbert in 2019, the players' union also requested and was granted the opportunity to meet with the league's final candidates.

A source familiar with the situation told ESPN that the league is approaching the process with an open mind -- recognizing that the WNBA is now at a point where a leader without a traditional background in the corporate world might offer advantages.

Building and managing relationships with players, as well as owners, executives and business leaders, is also seen as a priority following Engelbert's tenure, which notably included several strained relationships with key players

Since Engelbert's announcement Friday, people around the league have speculated about who might be part of the candidate pool. Here are some of the names ESPN has heard as possibilities.

Swin Cash

The former UConn star played in the WNBA from 2002 to 2016, winning three championships. Inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame in 2022, Cash has worked in the front office for the WNBA's New York Liberty (2017-19) and NBA's New Orleans Pelicans (2019-25). Cash, who turns 47 later this month, has also been a broadcast analyst. Her management experience is a plus, but some might question if Cash has spent enough time in the business world. -- Michael Voepel

Keia Clarke

She has been with the New York Liberty since 2011 and was promoted to CEO in 2020. She manages all business aspects of the franchise. Clarke played collegiate basketball at Canisius from 1999 to 2003 and began her career working for the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. Clarke, 45, then went to work for the WNBA/NBA league offices before joining the Liberty. She has postgraduate business degrees from NYU and Harvard. Clarke knows the ins and outs of a WNBA franchise business and has been part of the huge growth of the Liberty in the past seven years. -- Voepel

Bethany Donaphin

Currently head of WNBA operations, Donaphin has been with the league since 2016. She played at Stanford from 1998 to 2002, then competed professionally in the WNBA and overseas from 2002 to 2008. She earned an MBA in 2012 from Pennsylvania's Wharton School and then spent 2013 to 2016 at Deloitte, consulting for Fortune 500 companies. Donaphin, 46, has worked with former WNBA president Lisa Borders and Engelbert at the WNBA. One of the questions regarding Donaphis is whether her close ties to Engelbert during the past seven years would be seen as a negative by the players, considering their criticisms of Engelbert. -- Voepel

Tanya Hvizdak

A vice president of global sports marketing at Nike, Hvizdak has spent 25 years at the company. Nike is the outfitter for the WNBA and NBA, agreeing to a 12-year extension for that role in 2024. Hvizdak has been closely involved in the development and rollout of shoes for prominent WNBA athletes such as A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark and Sabrina Ionescu. Hvizdak also spearheaded a Nike think tank, which included Serena Williams and Ionescu, in 2022 that focused on issues faced by female athletes. Hvizdak played collegiate basketball, first at Rhode Island and then Bentley, where she earned an MBA. Hvizdak has worked hard to elevate women's athletics and has extensive marketing and business knowledge. Would she want to relocate across the country from Portland to New York and take on a different type of role running the WNBA? -- Voepel

Nneka Ogwumike

If one of Engelbert's weaknesses was developing relationships with players, that's Ogwumike's clear strength. The Stanford grad is well-respected as WNBPA president for 10 years, a tenure that includes representing the players for two CBA negotiations. If Ogwumike is interested in the role, it would be a fascinating and unprecedented turn coming less than a year removed from a contentious labor negotiation between the players' union and the league/owners; Ogwumike has built a legacy representing the former, but the commissioner's job is to represent the latter.

Ogwumike, who recently announced she'll be retiring from the WNBA at the end of the season, has been asked if she would be interested in being WNBA commissioner. She responded, "I don't close doors, but I do appreciate vacation. There is so much that I don't know, and there is so much that I would have to learn before even, if an opportunity like that were to come for me, to be ready for that." So perhaps it's more realistic that Ogwumike would seek some other experiences first before pursuing that sort of leadership role. Either way, the league could gauge her interest in taking a sort of liaison role where she'd serve as a bridge between the league office and teams/players. -- Philippou

Jess Smith

In a similar vein to Clarke, Smith would be someone coming from the business side of a WNBA franchise. She has been at the helm as team president of the massively successful Golden State Valkyries since 2024. On the court, the Valkyries surpassed expectations by becoming the league's first expansion team to make the playoffs in its inaugural season. According to CNBC, the Valkyries are the first women's sports team with a $1 billion valuation. Smith has two decades of experience in pro sports, with previous stops at the team level in the MLB, NHL, MLS and NWSL. -- Philippou

Mark Tatum

Tatum, who previously served as the league's interim president between Lisa Borders' and Engelbert's tenures, would be a surprise pick in some respects. The league has had only female leaders. And, as the longtime deputy commissioner and COO of the NBA, he would be seen as an extension of Silver, putting into question how much autonomy the WNBA really has as a separate entity from the NBA. But if Tatum is seriously considered, it might indicate Silver isn't interested in achieving that dynamic. -- Philippou

ESPN's Ramona Shelburne also contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc's advice for Max vs 100 drivers: Don't crash into Verstappen!
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their two pence on how they think the race will go down.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their predictions on how they think the race will go down.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Verstappen know each other very well on the karting track from years of battles when they were younger where they constantly fought for race wins.

Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and will be trying to overtake as many drivers as possible from the very back of the grid at Silverstone.

Leclerc has warned competitors that it would be "tough" to race against one of the best drivers of this generation, but to remember that he will have nine more rounds of the F1 season in front of him.

"I mean 100 [drivers] is a lot," he said.

"Ok, that would be fun. That would be cool. Honestly, the only advice I'll give is maybe not to crash into Max, because he's got a season to finish.

"And for Max to be careful, because I don't know how professional those drivers are, but 100 drivers is quite a lot on a track, so I think it would be fun.

"But obviously when you're racing against one of the best drivers in the world, they'll probably have a tough time."

This is unlike anything Verstappen has done before, and it will be taking place on a custom-built karting track in Silverstone on Sept. 16, just a few days after the Spanish Grand Prix.

Asked what he was most looking forward to about the live event, Verstappen said: "Just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me."

- Max vs 100: Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Spanish Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Madrid, how to watch

- Ferrari's vintage disaster-class paves way for Antonelli to win Italian GP

Mercedes' George Russell had a slightly different approach to taking on the Red Bull driver and advised that the competitors might need to be more tactical in order to keep the racing star behind.

Verstappen is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking and has four consecutive world championship titles to his name in F1.

"If you go full four abreast around the whole track he might be quite difficult to protect, so maybe a couple of drivers work as a team to try and block him," Russell advised.

The Englishman then found out that content creators and athletes will be racing against Verstappen, rather than professional racing drivers.

"He will be achieving that," Russell said. "I did a team race with 160 of my team members last week, and we had some top drivers, but yeah I think he should probably comfortably doing that task."

Max vs 100 will be broadcast live on Disney+ on Sept. 16.

stories.headline: Arena for 76ers, Flyers to open in 2030, marks 'new era'
stories.summary: The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new fully privately funded arena in South Philadelphia, which is targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030.
stories.body:
The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new arena on the former Spectrum site in South Philadelphia, which the organizations are calling the largest fully privately funded project in city history.

The arena is now targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030, when Philadelphia's expansion team will begin play. The Sixers, owned by Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE), come in as 50-50 partners with Comcast Spectacor in the new arena, after spending more than a decade as tenants.

"This is a new era for Philadelphia sports," Comcast chairman Brian Roberts said. "To build our future where Ed Snider and the Spectrum made history makes this project truly special. Working with HBSE, we are creating a world-class experience worthy of Philadelphia's incredible fans."

The Spectrum-inspired design includes more than a half-acre of outdoor gathering space, with fan plazas, food and beverage options and a large entrance staircase inspired by the steps at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

"Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that," Sixers managing partner Josh Harris said. "This privately funded arena will be the home to moments and memories that define this city for generations."

Added NBA commissioner Adam Silver: "I'm thrilled to see the first renderings of what promises to be an extraordinary home for NBA and WNBA basketball as well as many other world-class events. Beyond the incredible experience the new arena will bring to fans, I commend HBSE and Comcast for such a significant economic investment in Philadelphia."

For the Flyers, the move brings the franchise back to the grounds where it began play in 1967 and won its only two Stanley Cups.

Since taking over as Flyers governor in 2023, Dan Hilferty has also overseen a restructuring of Philadelphia's front office and made returning the franchise to consistent Stanley Cup contention a priority.

"This new arena will be a state-of-the-art home worthy of the Flyers, their fans, and the entire city," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "Comcast Spectacor and HBSE's commitment to this project reflects a shared belief in Philadelphia's future and a lasting investment in the city's economic vitality."

The organizations project the arena will create nearly 15,000 jobs and generate nearly $6 billion in economic activity over the next decade, along with hundreds of millions of dollars in new tax revenue benefiting the city and the School District of Philadelphia.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Griezmann catapults Orlando into the playoff picture
stories.summary: With eight goal contributions in eight games since joining the Lions, Antoine Griezmann has turned around Orlando's season. That and more in ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While Nashville dropped points in a 0-0 draw against New York City on Friday, their biggest competitors for the Supporters' Shield slipped up, too. Both Vancouver and Miami failed to win, leaving Nashville with a 10-point lead atop the Shield race.

2. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 2

Despite taking an early lead, the Whitecaps quickly crumbled in a 3-1 home defeat against St. Louis. In what was, perhaps, their worst match of the season, Vancouver fell apart before halftime en route to losing to fellow contender out West for the second time in four games.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 7

You couldn't have written a better script for St. Louis' Saturday night. Not only did new additions Rafael Navarro and Damion Downs make their debuts in the second half, but the visitors took the game to Vancouver and secured a 3-1 road victory. Doubt St. Louis' contender status at your own peril.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Miami's Achilles heel is widely known: they're a team that gets easily scrambled in their own third. With two sloppy fouls conceding two penalties to Atlanta, Saturday's 2-2 draw with the Five Stripes was the latest example of Inter Miami's defensive play letting them down.

5. LAFC
Previous ranking: 5

Despite holding a one-goal lead heading into the intermission, LAFC's second-half concession saw them earn just a point on the road against Salt Lake. An unwillingness -- or inability -- to keep the ball late in games continues to bite for the Black & Gold.

6. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 6

After their scheduled meeting with D.C. United was postponed due to inclement weather, Cincinnati will have extra time to bed in their defensive reinforcements. That 4-0 loss to Nashville last time out still stings.

7. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 4

The good news? Chicago bagged four goals on Saturday, including one from Robert Lewandowski as he continues to find his place in the attack. The bad news? Chicago conceded four in a 4-4 draw with Toronto. It's safe to say Chicago are missing rising star Mbekezeli Mbokazi in the backline.

8. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 9

Up against a fearsome Nashville team, New York City manager Pascal Jansen opted for a fairly conservative approach on Friday. Ceding most of the ball, the Pigeons did well to keep Nashville scoreless, but they failed to create much danger themselves in a 0-0 home draw.

9. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Trailing by two goals at halftime, the Revs couldn't find a way to equalize against the Galaxy on their way to a 2-1 road defeat. While Carles Gil's penalty conversion got them on the board, questions remain about whether the options New England have placed around him will produce.

10. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

Despite having a man advantage for the final 20-plus minutes of the match, Houston had a hard time creating much of anything in their 0-0 road draw with Charlotte. While attacking questions remain for Ben Olsen's outfit, the Dynamo's string of shutdown defensive showings mark them as a team that must be taken seriously.

11. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

While Charlotte couldn't find a breakthrough during their 0-0 home draw with Houston, Allan Saint-Maximin looked like the best player on the field. Dean Smith's new left winger was at the center of nearly every threatening move and has the look of an MLS star.

12. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 12

Still winless in league play since May, RSL drew 2-2 with LAFC on Saturday. They created a slew of quality chances, but also proved too open in defensive transition as control and tactical balance still eludes them.

13. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 16

Antoine Griezmann continued his absolute tear with the lone goal in Orlando's 1-0 win over San Diego. Now with eight goal contributions in eight games since debuting for the Lions, Griezmann has quickly turned around Orlando's season: they're now above the playoff line in the East.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

If there's a debate about MLS's best striker, Petar Musa is doing his best to end it. The Croatia international managed two goals, including the game winner, and an assist in Dallas' 4-3 win over Kansas City. While the home side's focus lacked, Musa's certainly didn't.

15. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 15

Since league play resumed after the World Cup, the Union are yet to lose. Saturday's 2-0 victory over Montréal lengthened that streak of results to eight games, with six of them going down as wins. With yet another goal from Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia are flying.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 15

Missing star midfielder Jeppe Tverskov due to a card suspension, San Diego's ball progression never turned into regular chances in a 1-0 road loss to Orlando. Without the Dane, the sophomore side simply can't carry the same threat going forward.

17. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 11

For a team that prides itself on effective defending, conceding three goals in the first half in a 5-4 loss to the Timbers was nowhere near good enough for Minnesota. Still, breakout striker Marcus Caldeira's brace could signal longer-term attacking improvement for a team fighting for a playoff spot.

18. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 20

The Galaxy marked Sergi Roberto's first MLS start with a 2-1 victory over New England. The former Barcelona man was a touch magnet in central midfield, helping his new team conduct play. If Roberto and Chucky Lozano, who notched an assist, maintain this form, the Galaxy won't be easily dismissed.

19. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Josh Sargent appears to be finding his form in MLS. While the U.S. striker had a quiet start to life in Toronto, he notched a hat trick in a 4-4 draw with Chicago over the weekend. It was a top-tier showing from Sargent atop Robin Fraser's attacking structure that led to a point for the hosts.

20. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

Now below the playoff line out East following a 0-0 draw in Seattle, that Red Bull New York didn't do more in the summer transfer window is a major concern. Without any game-changing additions made to the squad before deadline day, it's difficult to see how Michael Bradley's team will rebound.

21. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 21

On Saturday, Sounders fans could breathe a collective sigh of relief upon seeing Cristian Roldan make his first start for the team since May. Still, the USMNT midfielder's return wasn't enough to see Seattle claim their first win in months. A 0-0 draw with the Red Bulls had to suffice.

22. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 23

With star striker Kevin Kelsy now off to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership, replacement Vincent Janssen didn't waste any time filling the Venezuelan's shoes. Janssen notched a hat trick in the Timbers' wild 5-4 home win over Minnesota.

23. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 18

It looked as if the Quakes' winless run, one that stretches all the way back to May, was going to come to an end on Saturday. That is, until Austin managed a 97th-minute equalizer and a victory turned into a 1-1 draw for San Jose. The Earthquakes are in a bad, bad place.

24. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 24

D.C.'s meeting with Cincinnati was postponed due to weather, leaving the club without a chance to break a five-game winless streak.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Thanks to an equalizer from Guilherme Biro deep in second-half stoppage time, Austin secured a 1-1 draw against San Jose. The result marked four straight games without a loss in league play for the Texas capital club.

26. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 27

It didn't take Santi Rodriguez long to open his account in Columbus. The former New York City star bagged the opening goal for the Crew in a 3-0 victory over Colorado. With a remade attack, could this team make a late push for a spot in the postseason?

27. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 26

After trading Navarro to St. Louis and adding new pieces to the attack just before deadline day, the Rapids were nowhere near full strength in a 3-0 loss to the Crew. Colorado will have to wait for their new pieces to arrive and integrate to reach their full potential.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

At last, there are signs of life in Atlanta. During their 2-2 draw with Miami, new striker Breel Embolo made his debut and scored a late equalizer from the spot. Elsewhere, young defensive midfielder Mauricio Amaro made his first MLS appearance and looked extremely comfortable amid his new surroundings.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 29

Back to the bottom of the East after falling 2-0 in Philadelphia, it's difficult to see Montréal climbing the standings anytime soon. Even with Alexis Sánchez in the lineup, this team is still light on talent.

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 30

Although they managed one of their best attacking outings of the year, spurred on by new winger André Luiz's first start, Kansas City couldn't hold on for a point in Dallas. They fell 4-3 thanks to a late penalty by Musa.

stories.headline: PNG Chiefs secure record-breaking NRL sponsorship deal
stories.summary: The PNG Chiefs won't play an NRL game until 2028, but already the start-up club has netted the most lucrative sponsorship deal in the competition's history.
stories.body:
The PNG Chiefs won't play an NRL game until 2028, but already the start-up club has netted the most lucrative sponsorship deal in the competition's history.

The Chiefs announced on Wednesday that Bank South Pacific - which has branches throughout the Pacific - had agreed to a three-year deal to become the club's front-of-shirt sponsor.

The contract is believed to be worth about $15 million, averaging out at $5 million per season.

"This is a landmark partnership for the PNG Chiefs and Papua New Guinea and, as a club, we couldn't be prouder to welcome BSP on board," said Chiefs executive Lorna McPherson.

"To have this level of commitment to our club - including this period leading into our first game in 2028 - shows BSP's belief in what we are building, and the way we will create opportunities for Papua New Guineans for generations to come."

The acquisition of a major sponsor follows the club putting the first pieces of its roster together ahead of entry into the NRL in 2028.

The Chiefs have already signed Hull KR coach Willie Peters to lead them into their inaugural season, while also signing a who's who of high-profile names including Brian To'o, Jarome Luai, Zac Lomax, Alex Johnston and Joey Manu.
